sources.entry: Performance Monitor - Lightweight menu bar system monitor: CPU, memory, network, disk, GPU, per-sensor temperatures, SSD wear, and battery health. No telemetry.

summary.one_liner: A lightweight macOS menu bar app showing real-time CPU, memory, network, disk, GPU, battery, Bluetooth and thermal/fan readings in a popover, for Apple Silicon Macs.
summary.what_it_does: Shows live CPU usage with a per-process Top CPU list, where an app and its helper processes are grouped into one row and a glossary of 231 known processes explains what each one is. Memory view breaks down used, wired, compressed and free memory with a pressure indicator. Network view shows live throughput, a butterfly upload/download chart, VPN and connection indicators, local and public IPs, Wi-Fi SSID and signal strength, and read-only listening ports and open connections. Disk, GPU, battery and Bluetooth views cover I/O speeds, utilization, display info, battery health and cycle counts, and device battery levels. Thermal view reads CPU, GPU and battery temperatures and fan speeds from the SMC, with a menu bar readout and tiered history graphs kept for one hour, 48 hours and 90 days. It can also write a JSON snapshot for status bar tools and offers a small always-on-top floating panel.
use_cases: monitor CPU and memory usage from the macOS menu bar
check which app is using the CPU or network
watch Mac temperature and fan speed
see battery health and cycle count on a MacBook
check Bluetooth device battery levels such as AirPods
feed system metrics into SwiftBar, xbar or SketchyBar
keep an always-visible temperature readout over full-screen apps
how_to_run: Alternatively, download Performance Monitor.app from the GitHub Releases page and drag it to /Applications
Right-click the app and choose Open on first launch (ad-hoc signed)
Building from source: git clone the repository, cd performancemonitor, then run: bash build_app.sh
notable: No telemetry or analytics; the app makes only three network requests (update check, optional public-IP lookup, latency probe to a host you choose)
Thermal and fan readings come from the SMC via IOKit across M1 to M4 chips
Tiered history storage at one-second, one-minute and one-hour resolutions with sleep, wake and throttling events marked on graphs
Floating panel stays visible over full-screen apps and holds nothing while hidden
Process glossary with 231 entries in seven languages
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon (M1 or later); the build is arm64-only and will not run on Intel Macs
Ad-hoc signed without an Apple Developer ID, so first launch needs right-click Open to bypass Gatekeeper
